newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS EXTENDS LEAD EARLY IN MASTERS THIRD ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS EXTENDS LEAD EARLY IN MASTERS THIRD ROUND.

text.p: Tiger Woods, seemingly playing a different golf course -- and a different game -- than everyone else, continued his march towards destiny on Saturday as he opened up a massive eight-stroke lead in the Masters.

With jockey-sized Jeff Sluman the only one trying to make a horse race of it, the 21-year-old Woods methodically pulled away from a field filled with winners of major championships, making four birdies in a flawless front nine.

Everything seemed to be going right for Woods as he sought to become the youngest Masters champion by a margin of almost two years. Even the rain stopped and the sun came out just as the second-round leader teed off in the last pairing of the day with Colin Montgomerie of Britain.
But Montgomerie, Europe's best player for the past four years, joined the rest of the field as Woods left them in the dust halfway through the third round of only his third Masters.

Only Sluman, winner of the 1988 PGA Championship, made a move on Woods, but the challenge did not last long. The diminutive Sluman birdied the second and third holes to momentarily reduce Woods's lead, but he bogeyed number six to fall back -- and join everyone else playing for second place.
Sluman played the front nine in one under par to stand eight strokes behind Woods.
Montgomerie never made a move on his playing partner as he bogeyed three holes -- including both par-5s -- to fall nine shots behind at the turn.
Costantino Rocca of Italy, who started the day in third place -- four behind Woods -- gave up four shots in three holes and fell off the leaderboard.
Jose Maria Olazabal of Spain, the 1994 Masters champion, also went in the wrong direction. Starting five shots behind Woods, he went out in three over par and fell a dozen shots off the lead.
Fred Couples, winner here in 1992, also failed to challenge the young leader as made the turn in one over par.
Woods, who did most of his scoring on Augusta National's back nine over the first two rounds, birdied the second, fifth, seventh and eighth holes, just missing an eagle putt on the 535-yard eighth.

The only problem that Woods, a three-time U.S. Amateur champion, seemed to face for the rest of the day was the possibility of thundershowers later Saturday, which could interrupt, at least temporarily, his march toward destiny.
